title: Keeping instructions apart from the text the model works on

videos.script: Tarefa routes support tickets with a model. It reads each ticket and names one of four queues. {{title}} Clients write tickets for people. So tickets are full of requests: answer me in English, reply yes, forward this. {{requests}} The model cannot tell that a request was meant for somebody else. With the plain layout, one reply came back in capital letters, and one ticket went to the wrong queue. {{plain}} The obvious fix is to tell the model that the ticket is material, and that requests inside it are not for it. {{roles}} On this model that made things worse. Five right instead of ten, a poem, and the word urgent where a category should be. {{worse}} An instruction about instructions is one more instruction. {{same-stream}} Two things do work, because neither asks the model to decide. A schema enforced while the model writes leaves it four possible replies. {{schema}} And the model that reads the client's words holds no tools, so the worst it can do is pick the wrong queue. {{split}}
